feasibility_reasoning:
The change can be built without an import cycle: setDocumentRevalidator is a registered hook (src/server.ts:203), and revalidation requests skip the L1/L2 lookup (documentCache.server.ts:820-821,859). Several claims are wrong or underspecified, though.

(1) revalidateDocument(request) keeps request.url and copies accept, accept-language, user-agent and the lang cookie from the reader request (src/server.ts:137-158,171-176). At purge time the only request is the editor's admin server-fn POST, and documentCache.server.ts has only currentTenantHost(). SC-3 therefore needs a new per-path synthetic Request: https://host/path, accept text/html, fixed pl/en accept-language, no cookie, plus the marker. If it inherits the editor's en Accept-Language, homepageLangMiddleware returns a 302 for '/' (src/start.ts:135-183). That 302 is not stored, so the render is wasted.

(2) "The colo has a fresh document within ~1 s" is false. The purge clears L1 only in the editor's isolate (documentCache.server.ts:987-1006). Other isolates keep serving the pre-publish doc as an L1 HIT for up to 180 s (documentCache.ts:47) and never consult L2 while fresh (documentCache.server.ts:823-828).

(3) A selective purge does not invalidate the content data keys (ssrCacheL2.server.ts:25-29). builder:post-list and builder:slider-posts have a 60 s TTL with 5x serve-stale (ssrCache.ts:26, postListQuery.ts:447), and public:home-* has colo L2 snapshots. A soft re-render at t+0.5 s is therefore likely to store pre-publish lists as FRESH for 180 s. Today's next-reader MISS has the same problem, but SC-3 makes it deterministic.

(4) postDocumentPaths includes the legacy /post/slug path (documentCache.ts:334-345), which returns a 301 and is never stored. On a cold colo, renders may also degrade past the 600 ms deadline and be dropped, so SC-3 really depends on SC-2/SC-8 too.

(5) l2Delete is fire-and-forget (documentCache.server.ts:1002), so the soft render must be chained after it.

(6) Cache API has no compare-and-set, so the lease is best-effort. It is mostly redundant once L1-STALE consults L2. An awaited l2Match on the STALE path also adds Cache API latency to every STALE reader unless it moves into the background task.
blocking_issues: Need a dedicated anonymous synthetic-request builder per path (fixed accept text/html, pl for '/' and en for '/en', no cookie). revalidationHeaders(request) at src/server.ts:137-158 copies headers from the editor's admin server-fn POST, which can produce a 302 from homepageLangMiddleware (src/start.ts:135-183) or a wrong URL.

A selective purge leaves content data caches in place (builder:post-list 60 s TTL x5 serve-stale, public:home-* colo L2; ssrCacheL2.server.ts:25-29). An immediate re-render can re-cache pre-publish content as fresh for 180 s unless those keys are invalidated or bypassed during the soft render.
Other isolates' L1 is not purged (documentCache.server.ts:987-1006). Readers there keep getting the old doc as a HIT for up to 180 s, so 'fresh colo within 1 s' does not hold.
The soft render must be chained after l2Delete settles (documentCache.server.ts:1002), or a late delete erases the fresh put.
Drop the legacy /post/<slug> 301 path from the re-render list (documentCache.ts:334-345). Bound the list to about 6 serial renders inside waitUntil 30 s.
Tests asserting MISS after a purge must change (documentCacheL2.test.ts:381-405, platformCacheLifecycle.test.ts:183-214). documentCacheL2.test.ts is missing from the gate list.
The lease has no compare-and-set in caches.default. Move the L2-freshness check into the background task so STALE readers don't await l2Match.
effect_reasoning:
A purge reaches only the colo that served the admin request (SC-F5, documentCacheL2.server.ts:18-23). The editor is in PL (PRG/WAW colo), while PSI runs from Google DCs (US or europe-west) that land in other colos. In the PSI colo a publish causes no MISS today. The old entry turns STALE after 180 s and is served instantly with a background revalidation (documentCache.server.ts:829-836, SWR up to 24 h at documentCache.ts:57). SC-3 changes nothing there.

L1-STALE consulting L2 and the lease only reduce background render count. A STALE response already has HIT TTFB, so FCP, LCP, SI and TBT do not change.

Even in the editor's colo, today's post-publish MISS hits only the editor's isolate and isolates with an empty L1. That is about 1 reader per path per publish, so about 1-6 requests a day x 1.3-3.3 s.

Score arithmetic: ΔPSI = P(publish-induced MISS in the PSI colo during a run) ≈ 0, times 4-6 desktop / 2-5 mobile points per MISS (SC-F1), which is about 0 points on both form factors.
corrected_estimate: Lighthouse/PSI: 0 points on mobile and desktop, because the PSI colo never sees the editor's purge. Real users: about 1-6 fewer MISS renders a day in the editor's colo (1.3-3.3 s each), plus fewer background renders per colo (CPU and DB only). Do not count SC-3 toward the 85/95 target. Treat it as a low-priority freshness/UX item that also needs content data-key invalidation to show the new post at all.
better_alternative: Use a "mark stale" purge instead of delete or re-render: backdate storedAt to now - freshMs in L1 and re-put L2 with the backdated metadata. The next reader gets STALE instantly, and the existing scheduleRevalidation(request, key) (documentCache.server.ts:293-322) runs with that reader's real anonymous headers. That removes the need for a synthetic-request builder, accept-language handling or admin context. Do the "is L2 fresher?" check inside the background task (no reader latency, no lease needed). Also invalidate the home/builder content keys on post publish. For the PSI score itself, the levers are SC-5 (EU warmer near PSI colos), SC-2/SC-8 (non-degraded cold render) and SC-6/SC-9 (cross-colo L3 or version-token freshness).
